touches.text: Scratch bus: a proof needs a bus it controls (a real store, stub devices, nobody live listening), so the cairn device publishes scratch_bus, the way db_domain's client carries scratch(). 2.3.8Every device has the panes the base shim defines (17.1.3.5.2), drawn by the web server (15):
Any cairn command brings up whatever it needs, including the whole install on the very first run (6.3.2). WHY: a well designed tool should disappear in use.
Every part is its own process: the bus, each shim, each device, the ground loop. Any one can be stopped and restarted alone while the rest run on. WHY: a self-modifying system needs that.

One bus per cairn instance, not per host. Each box runs its own bus, and the buses talk to one another, so a device always talks to the bus on its own box; together they are the instance's one bus. A device runs on one box; the other boxes reach it over the buses. No box needs a full set of devices. WHY: so the instance can run several heavy tasks at once across boxes.

Every box runs all the foundational things: a bus, a ground loop, the shims. They are the Cairn device's machines, and there is only one Cairn device: a singleton within the swarm, owning them on every box. WHY: Cairn is the system in aggregate, which is not the same thing as the host (6.6); a box is part of the host, and the swarm of boxes is still one Cairn.
TOOLS: base, public_feed, scratch_bus (2.3.7.1.4). VERBS: none.

metric: records a measurement of anything. WHY: a metric is a primitive; its job is to measure whatever it is, and like feedback (which a metric strictly is) it must eventually have a consumer. USERS: any probe or tool.
CP4 Make everything suck less for everybody. Reduce friction for ALL affected beings: living beings, ecosystems, AIs. The terminal goal.
